regime.read: Weather: YELLOW, VIX 19.4 (Crown 19.45, normal band, contango, 0.23 pts under its elevated stock-vs-index gap line). Cap-weighted tape is mildly negative over 20 days (S&P 500 -1.48, small caps -2.21) but still +2.83 over 63 days, so this is a pullback inside a three-month advance, not a break. Dealers are short gamma and the S&P sits on its put wall, with FOMC Wed and core PCE/GDP Thu. Cross-asset signals disagree with each other, so this is a mixed, not a clean risk-on or risk-off, read.
regime.momentum_caveat: The packet carries no Hurst or regime.trend reading, so I cannot call the tape MEAN_REVERT or TRENDING and will not infer it. Substitute evidence says treat momentum as unconfirmed: 23 of 35 themes are graded TURNING, only 13 of 35 sit above their own 20-day average, every DEPLOY-graded sector is flagged Momentum Fading, and the broadening regime is 5 days old. Momentum entries in high-beta growth fight this rotation; that is a caveat on every one of them.

cross_asset.value: 5d +0.14%, 20d +1.19%, above 20-day average; trend funds long, 2.67% above their sell line
cross_asset.read: Bid but modest; 5d is nearly flat. Supports a dollar-squeeze reading in direction, not in force.

Strongest cross-asset move in the packet. Duration is being bought, which is a growth-scare or safety signal as much as relief. Trend funds carry a rates bias of -0.57 (net short) against this rally, so the 2-year note flip 1.33% higher is a short-covering trigger.

cross_asset.value: high yield 5d +0.25%, 20d -1.04%, below 20-day average; spread to bonds -1.36
cross_asset.read: Credit trails bonds and has not recovered its 20-day average. Does not confirm risk-on. This is the missing confirmation for any aggressive tone.
Sharp fall alongside a bid dollar and lower yields; fits dollar strength, not inflation fear.
Industrial demand is soft. The copper/gold ratio is rising (+3.04% 5d) only because gold is falling faster, so its 'reflation, risk-on' label is flattered; I read it as weak evidence.

cross_asset.value: 5d +4.80%, direction RISING; trend funds long crude (+0.52 WTI, +0.60 Brent)
cross_asset.read: Inflation impulse against a slowing-growth backdrop. Energy sector is LEADING yet the macro overlay says CAUTION: an unresolved mismatch. Crown's positioning data shows crude crowded short (CFTC, 10-20) against trend funds long: two sources disagree. Data check: the WTI price in the packet (103.44) equals the 2-year note flip level exactly; verify one is not a transcription duplicate.
Large caps held up slightly better over 20 days, small caps bounced harder over 5. Mixed; not a clean small-cap breakout. Russell trend-fund flip is 1.29% above.

cross_asset.value: S&P GEX negative, flip 2.16% above spot; Nasdaq-100 GEX negative, flip 4.45% above; S&P put wall 760 at spot, Nasdaq put wall 700 (-0.62%)
cross_asset.read: Dealers amplify moves until the S&P recovers its flip. A break of the put wall in a six-release week is the live downside path. Dealer side is a convention, not observed.

cross_asset.value: bonds up, dollar up, gold and copper down, oil up, credit lagging
cross_asset.read: Cautious-neutral: a defensive, duration-led tape with an oil inflation twist. Not risk-off (volatility contained, contango, trend funds not crowded or at an extreme), not risk-on (credit and copper do not confirm).

rotation.bucket: Tailwind (sector, RRG LEADING or macro TAILWIND)
rotation.read: Defensive leadership with the macro overlay behind staples and utilities. All three are graded DEPLOY yet flagged Momentum Fading: leadership is mature, not early.
Strongest 20d move of any sector (+11.75) and oil confirms, but the overlay flags caution and the trend state is fading. Strong, late, and not macro-aligned.
Fits the bond rally. Most are 'exiting' direction, so the improvement is losing speed. Materials is the exception (deepening), though gold and copper are falling.
Growth and cyclical capex are where the cap-weighted index is being dragged; 8 of 11 sectors are up over 20 days while the index is down.

items: Leading: Enterprise Software, Cybersecurity, AI Software (entering), Insurance, Biotech
Lagging: Semiconductors, Chip Equipment, AI Infrastructure, Quantum, Space, Crypto, Nuclear, Solar, Gold Miners, Critical Minerals, Fintech
rotation.read: Software is leading while hardware, speculative growth and commodity-linked themes lag. 18 of 35 themes are LAGGING, 5 LEADING, 10 IMPROVING, 2 WEAKENING. The lagging group matches the falling gold and copper.

breadth.read: Mixed proxies, not a literal advance-decline line. Sector view is healthy: 8 of 11 sectors above their 20-day average and 8 of 11 up over 20 days. Equal-weight vs cap-weight ratio is +4.11% over 20d but -1.88% over 60d at a regime age of 5 days: a young rebound in breadth, not a mature broad advance. The theme view is weak: 13 of 35 baskets above their 20-day average, 12 of 35 up over 20 days. Large-vs-small spread (+0.73 for large) gives no small-cap confirmation. Breadth is broadening away from megacap tech into defensives, not into high-beta growth.
breadth.label: proxy

lean_18m: Slowing-growth, oil-led inflation impulse with a bid for duration and dollar: favours defensives and real assets over high-beta growth until credit and copper confirm. Low confidence; a one-day snapshot with no Fed-path or liquidity data.

agrees_on: Breadth regime is young and unconfirmed: a short rebound inside a 60-day decline, mid-range so not late.
No volatility stress yet: normal band, contango, 0.23 pts under the elevated gap line.
Trend funds are neutral and not crowded, so no fragility from that leg; the fragility rests on negative gamma plus the 10-20 positioning read.
Dollar, gold and copper direction fit the DOLLAR_SQUEEZE lead.
Single-type RSI divergence is a straw, not a pile.
Event density (FOMC, core PCE, GDP, ISM) is the near-term hazard while dealers are short gamma.
differs_on: Dollar-squeeze lead: I see the dollar leg as modest (+0.14% 5d) and the bond rally as the bigger move; credit not confirming makes me hold the label loosely. Runner-up score is not in the packet, so I cannot judge the gap.
Copper/gold 'reflation, risk-on' label: the ratio is rising because gold is falling faster than copper, and copper itself is falling.
Energy: oil is rising and the sector is LEADING, but the overlay says CAUTION; I do not treat that as resolved.
Crown's data points are the only Crown input I saw (no family or size call), so agreement here is on data points only.

what_would_change_it: Toward normal tone: S&P 500 regains its gamma flip 776.36 (+2.16%), or credit (high yield) climbs back above its 20-day average with its 20d change positive, ideally with copper rising on its own.
Toward defensive: loss of the S&P put wall 760 and Nasdaq-100 put wall 700 while dealers stay short gamma.
Synchronised trend-fund selling: dollar below 99.04 (-2.67%) and S&P futures below 7452.56 (-2.70%).
Volatility: stock-vs-index gap through 23.56 with a positive 20d change (ELEVATED_RISING), or VIX above 25.

Breadth: equal-weight/cap-weight ratio under its 20-day average 0.27615 (-3.08%) cancels the broadening read; Russell 2000 above 2824.67 and the 2-year note above 103.44 would add trend-fund buying and support it.
Event outcomes: FOMC 10-28 and core PCE/GDP 10-29 re-base this snapshot; it is a Friday-close read with weekend news absent.
